patch.value: Investigate mixed-writer delivery SLO on an isolated capacity host

The capacity harness measured 100 distinct authenticated subscribers, 10 mixed writer lanes and 50 committed updates after the late-fact replay repair. All 5000 deliveries arrived with zero loss or duplicates, but to-all p99 was 2163.5 ms against a 2000 ms SLO. The ladder correctly stopped before 1000 subscribers. High host scheduling or I/O pressure was observed without a proven saturated server resource. Reproduce from docs/capacity/2026-10-15-local.md on an isolated host; compare service, writer and storage timing before changing production limits. Related feature pm-web-lh4b and companion pm-cli-website-ghe1. Larger rungs and hosted capacity remain unmeasured.

value.author: codex-agent
value.text: DRAFT UPSTREAM ISSUE (not filed). Title: Mixed history-index readers and writers can delay authoritative append beyond a 2-second delivery budget. Package: @unbrained/pm-cli 2026.10.15. Reproduce with the public pm-web capacity harness, disposable test Postgres, 100 authenticated SSE readers, five HTTP SDK writer lanes and five separate pinned CLI writer lanes, five independent item updates each; retain ordinary 250 ms mutation polling and 60-second inclusive replay. docs/capacity/2026-10-16-local.md records three untraced p99 values 1181.3/898.9/913.2 ms and three traced values 633.9/2965.8/1239.2 ms. In the breached run, all 50 updates and 5000 receipts arrived exactly once. CLI timestamp-to-authoritative-append p99/max 2247.5 ms independently exceeds the total 2000 ms SLO; index-file-lock wait lower bound p99/max is 2071.0 ms. Detecting SDK read/classification p99 1106.7 ms, polling wait p99 232.4 ms; per-client write p99 under 0.05 ms. Implementation inspection: queryHistoryEventIndex and appendHistoryEntryWithEventIndex both acquire withHistoryEventIndexLock; append acquires before authoritative history write and queries validate stream sizes under that exclusive lock. Expected: committed-fact readers should not introduce unbounded writer latency or visibility loss. Investigate a validated nonblocking/read snapshot strategy or fair lock acquisition while preserving authoritative fallback and late-fact visibility; do not remove validation or timestamp overlap blindly. Clock starts before persistence by harness contract, not at fsync or response. Shared-host scheduling and probe perturbation remain confounders; reader-versus-writer contention contribution and the original busy-host breach are not separately proven. No upstream mutation or filing performed.
